adminOnly: Only the admin can manage integrations.
adminOnlySignIn: Only the admin can change sign-in settings.
adminOnlyApiKeys: Only the admin can manage API keys.
adminOnlyTraktImport: Only the admin can import from Trakt.
adminOnlyDiscover: Only the admin can arrange Discover.
apiKeyGone: That API key doesn't exist any more.
connectTmdbFirst: Connect TMDb in Settings → Integrations first.
pageIntro: Connect your own Plex, Jellyfin, Sonarr, and Radarr so Marquee knows what you already own and can send the rest straight to your download queue. Credentials are encrypted and only ever used on your behalf.
name: Name
librarySummary: {movies, plural, one {# movie} other {# movies}} · {shows, plural, one {# TV show} other {# TV shows}}
apiKeysIntro: Let dashboards like Homepage or Homarr, scripts and other apps use Marquee. A key works like signing in, so keep it secret. Read-only keys can look but not change anything; no key can manage keys or these settings. <link>API reference</link>
apiKeyCopyNow: Copy this key now — it won't be shown again.
apiKeyRevokeConfirm: Revoke “{name}”? Anything using it stops working straight away.
apiKeyActAsHint: A key acting as a member can only do what they can — right for an app that just makes requests.
apiKeyLastUsedMinutes: {count, plural, one {Last used # minute ago} other {Last used # minutes ago}}
apiKeyLastUsedHours: {count, plural, one {Last used # hour ago} other {Last used # hours ago}}
apiKeyLastUsedDays: {count, plural, one {Last used # day ago} other {Last used # days ago}}
arrIntro: Add as many servers as you run. Titles go to the default one unless you pick another under “Advanced” when approving or adding. A title on any standard server counts as in your library; 4K servers take 4K requests.
apiKeySavedPlaceholder: Saved — enter a new one to replace it
arrReenterApiKey: Enter the API key again to change the URL.
arrUsedWhenAdded: Used when a title is added to this server:
arrAnimeIntro: For anime (TMDb says it's anime, or it's animation from Japan) — added as series type “Anime”:
arrWebhookHelp: In {app} → Settings → Connect → Add → Webhook, paste this (method POST, on Grab and on Import).
noSonarrYet: No Sonarr yet — add one to send shows straight to your download queue.
noRadarrYet: No Radarr yet — add one to send movies straight to your download queue.
discordIntro: Posts a message to a Discord channel for the events picked above.
discordPlaceholder: From a channel's Integrations → Webhooks settings in Discord
discordSuccess: Connected — check the channel for a test message.
ntfyIntro: Sends a push notification to your phone or desktop via ntfy.sh (or a self-hosted ntfy server) for the events picked above. Members can pick their own topic on this server.
ntfySuccess: Connected — check the topic for a test message.
customWebhookIntro: Posts a JSON payload ({payload}) to any URL for the events picked above — for your own automation or a self-hosted notification gateway.
customWebhookSuccess: Connected — check your endpoint for a test request.
sharedWebhooksIntro: Each Sonarr and Radarr server above has its own webhook URL now (under Edit) — use that for new servers. These older shared URLs keep working for servers already set up with them: pasted into Radarr/Sonarr → Settings → Connect → Add → Webhook (method POST, trigger on Grab + Download), they tell you here as soon as something starts or finishes downloading.
householdEventsIntro: The channels below are the household's: everything picked here goes to each one that's set up, once. Members can add their own Telegram, Pushover, email, Discord, ntfy or webhook under Settings › Account › Notifications, using the bot, app and mail server set up here.
jellyfinIntro: Emby speaks the same language as Jellyfin, so either works here.
jellyfinIntroConnected: Emby speaks the same language as Jellyfin, so either works here — connected to {name}.
jellyfinApiKeyHelp: Generate an API key from the dashboard: Administration → API Keys in Jellyfin, or Advanced → API Keys in Emby.
channelTelegramIntro: Posts to a Telegram chat, group or channel through your own bot for the events picked above. Members can use it for their own notifications too.
channelTelegramSuccess: Connected — check the chat for a test message.
botTokenHint: Message @BotFather on Telegram, send /newbot, and paste the token it gives you.
chatIdHint: Send your bot a message (or add it to the group), then open {url} to find the chat's id.
channelPushoverIntro: Sends a push notification through Pushover for the events picked above. Members can use it for their own notifications too.
channelPushoverSuccess: Connected — a test notification is on its way.
appTokenHint: Create an application at pushover.net/apps/build and copy its API token.
userKeyHint: Your user key is at the top of your pushover.net dashboard.
channelEmailIntro: Emails one or more addresses through your own mail server (SMTP) for the events picked above. Members can use it for their own notifications too.
channelEmailSuccess: Connected — check the inbox for a test email.
portHint: 587 for most servers; 465 with “Secure connection” on.
usernamePlaceholder: Leave blank if the server needs none
passwordHint: For Gmail, an app password (myaccount.google.com/apppasswords), not your normal one.
sendToHint: One or more addresses, separated by commas.
secureConnection: Secure connection from the start (TLS, usually port 465)
plexTimedOut: Timed out waiting for Plex sign-in. Try again.
librarySynced: Your library is kept in sync automatically.
plexSignInPrompt: Sign in with your Plex account to see what's already in your library.
plexFinishSignIn: Finish signing in in the tab that just opened.
ssoIntro: Adds “Sign in with …” for your own identity provider — Authentik, Authelia, Pocket ID, Keycloak, Google, or anything else that speaks OpenID Connect — on the website and the Mac and Windows apps.
ssoButtonNameHint: The name on the sign-in button, as in “Sign in with Authentik”.
ssoPublicUrlHint: The address people use to reach Marquee from outside.
ssoRedirectUri: Redirect URI — add this to the provider exactly
ssoIssuerHint: The provider's issuer, or its …/.well-known/openid-configuration address.
ssoPublicClient: Leave empty for a public client
ssoRemoveSecret: Remove the saved secret (a public client)
ssoScopesHint: Add “groups” for Authelia and Pocket ID if you use groups below.
ssoAllowSignupHint: Anyone your provider lets in gets a member account on first sign-in. Off: only accounts that linked it can use it.
ssoMatchEmail: Match existing accounts by verified email
ssoMatchEmailHint: First sign-in links an account whose username is the person's email — only when the provider says the email is verified, and never the admin account.
ssoRequiredGroupHint: Only people in this group can sign in with it.
ssoTrustedGroupHint: Members in this group become Trusted when they sign in. Nobody is ever made an admin this way.
ssoSaved: Saved. The sign-in button is live.
tmdbIntro: Shared for this whole Marquee instance, not just your account.
tmdbPlaceholder: v3 API key or v4 access token, from themoviedb.org/settings/api
traktIntro: Import a public Trakt list or watchlist as requests — doesn't require Trakt sign-in, just a free API app.
traktPlaceholder: From a Trakt API app at trakt.tv/oauth/applications
traktImportHint: Also works with a watchlist URL (e.g. .../users/username/watchlist). The list must be public on Trakt's side. Matching titles not already owned or requested get added to your pending Requests queue.
traktImportedSkipped: {count, plural, one {Imported # title} other {Imported # titles}} ({skipped, plural, one {# skipped} other {# skipped}} — already owned or requested).
tvdbIntro: Fills in poster art and an overview for TV shows when TMDb doesn't have them yet — Sonarr's own metadata comes from here too.
discoverIntro: The rows on Discover, for everyone in the household. Move them, hide the ones nobody uses, and add your own — a TMDb keyword, genre, studio, network or list, a Trakt list, or what's new in your library.
shelfKindKeywordHint: Everything TMDb tags with a keyword, like “anime” or “time travel”.
shelfKindGenreHint: The most popular movies or series in one genre.
shelfKindCompanyHint: A production company's titles, like A24 or Studio Ghibli.
shelfKindNetworkHint: Series from one network or streaming service.
shelfKindTmdbListHint: A public list on themoviedb.org, by its number or link.
shelfKindTraktListHint: A public list or watchlist on trakt.tv, by its link.
shelfKindLibraryHint: What's new on your Plex or Jellyfin server.
filterNetworks: Filter networks, or a TMDb network number
pickSourceFirst: {kind, select, keyword {Pick a TMDb keyword first.} genre {Pick a genre first.} company {Pick a studio first.} other {Pick a network first.}}
traktNotConnected: Trakt isn't connected yet — connect it in Settings → Integrations, or this row stays empty.
changesApply: Changes apply to Discover straight away, for everyone.
resetConfirm: Put the built-in rows back as they were?
maxCustomRows: {count, plural, one {Discover has # row of your own, the most it can have. Remove it to add another.} other {Discover has # rows of your own, the most it can have. Remove one to add another.}}
omdbIntro: Optional. With a key, title pages show IMDb, Rotten Tomatoes and Metacritic scores beside TMDb's.
publicUrlHelp: Where "Play on Jellyfin" opens when people reach the server at a different address than Marquee does.
regionLanguageIntro: Which country streaming providers and release dates are for, and where and in what language TMDb's Popular and Upcoming rows are picked from.
streamingRegionHelp: "Currently streaming on" and a movie's theatrical and digital release dates are for this country.
discoverRegionHelp: Popular Movies and Upcoming Movies are picked for this country.
discoverLanguageHelp: The original language Popular, Upcoming and the Movies and Series pages are limited to. "Any language" lifts the limit.
